lblName: Performance: take-off speeds and fuel, the climbs, the cruise and a turn calculator, for your F-16, its load and the departure field's weather. The take-off figures go to the DataCard.
grpAirport: Airport: the field you take off from, its runway and the take-off weather (temperature, wind, QNH). Type over the weather to try other conditions.
grpAircraft: Aircraft: which F-16 block, its weights, fuel and drag. The loadout comes from the briefing or the save; Set opens the Loadout window to change it here.
grpTakeOff: TakeOff: the speeds for your weight, pitch and thrust on this runway: rotation, lift-off and refusal. They go to the DataCard.
grpEngineInfo: Engine Info: the engine of the F-16 picked, its thrust and the MIL power setting to check on the take-off roll.
grpExlpanation: How to read the climb figures: the speed to hold, then the distance, fuel and time to reach the altitude picked under Cruise.
grpMaxABClimb: MAX AB Climb: climbing in full afterburner from the field to the altitude picked under Cruise: the speed to hold, distance, fuel and time.
grpMILClimb: MIL Climb: climbing at MIL power (full power without afterburner) to the altitude picked under Cruise: speed, distance, fuel and time.
grpCruise: Cruise: the best-range Mach and altitudes for your weight and drag. Pick which altitude the climb figures are worked out to.
grpInput: Turn calculator, Input: speed, altitude, G and temperature of a turn. Change any of them to see the result below.
grpResult: Turn calculator, Result: true airspeed, Mach, the temperatures, density altitude and the turn radius for the Input above.
btnSelect: Picks another airfield of the theater for the take-off figures. The page opens on your flight's departure field, from the briefing or the save.
btnChart: Shows this airfield's charts: the ground chart the app draws from BMS's own airfield data, a parking chart per runway end, then its instrument charts. Greyed where there are none.
lblAPT_VAL: The airfield the take-off figures are for: your flight's departure field, or the one picked with Select APT.
lblIcao: The airfield's ICAO code, from the app's airport data for this theater.
lblRWY: The runway end you take off from. It opens on the end most nearly into the take-off wind (or the DataCard's departure runway); the head and cross wind are for it.
cboRWY: The runway end you take off from. It opens on the end most nearly into the take-off wind (or the DataCard's departure runway); the head and cross wind are for it.
lblELV: The field's elevation, feet MSL, from BMS's ATC data or else the ground under the runways. With the QNH it gives the pressure altitude the take-off charts use.
lblELV_Val: The field's elevation, feet MSL, from BMS's ATC data or else the ground under the runways. With the QNH it gives the pressure altitude the take-off charts use.
lblTODA: Take-off distance available, feet and metres: the runway's length in BMS's data. The refusal speed is worked out for it less 150 ft.
lblTODA_Val: Take-off distance available, feet and metres: the runway's length in BMS's data. The refusal speed is worked out for it less 150 ft.
lblLDA: Landing distance available, feet and metres: the runway's length in BMS's data.
lblLDA_Val: Landing distance available, feet and metres: the runway's length in BMS's data.
lblWidth: The runway's width, feet and metres, from BMS's own runway outline. For information: no figure uses it.
lblWidth_Val: The runway's width, feet and metres, from BMS's own runway outline. For information: no figure uses it.
lblAPT_Temp: The field's temperature at take-off, °C: the briefing's or the weather file's, or type your own. It sets the take-off factor and the climb figures.
txtTemp: The field's temperature at take-off, °C: the briefing's or the weather file's, or type your own. It sets the take-off factor and the climb figures.
lblISA_Dev: How far the field's temperature is from a standard day at its elevation, °C (15 °C at sea level, 2 °C colder per 1,000 ft). The climb figures are corrected for it.
lblWind: The take-off wind: direction in degrees (0-359), then speed in knots (0-200), from the briefing or the weather file. Type to change either.
txtWindDir: The take-off wind's direction, degrees (0-359), from the briefing or the weather file. With the speed it gives the head and cross wind on the runway.
txtWindSpd: The take-off wind's speed, knots (0-200). With the direction it gives the head and cross wind on the runway.
lblHWC: Headwind on the runway picked, knots (a minus is a tailwind). It corrects the refusal speed.
lblCWC: Crosswind on the runway picked, knots.
lblQNH: The altimeter setting, in hPa and inches of mercury: from the weather, else 1013.2 / 29.92. With the elevation it gives the pressure altitude for take-off.
txtQNH_Hpa: The altimeter setting, hPa (914-1050); the inches box follows when you leave it. From the weather, else 1013.2.
txtQNH_In: The altimeter setting, inches of mercury (27.00-31.00); the hPa box follows when you leave it.
lblType: The F-16 the figures are for: your flight's jet. Pick another block to compare; your stores go across to it, and picking the mission's jet brings its loadout back.
cboType: The F-16 the figures are for: your flight's jet. Pick another block to compare; your stores go across to it, and picking the mission's jet brings its loadout back.
lblEmpty: The jet's empty weight, lb, from Falcon BMS's aircraft data for this theater, with the conformal tanks when the jet carries them.
lblEmpty_Val: The jet's empty weight, lb, from Falcon BMS's aircraft data for this theater, with the conformal tanks when the jet carries them.
lblLoadout: What the stores, pylons and racks weigh, lb: the briefing's loadout, or what you set in the Loadout window (Set).
lblLoadout_val: What the stores, pylons and racks weigh, lb: the briefing's loadout, or what you set in the Loadout window (Set).
btnLoadout: Opens the Loadout window: the stores on each hardpoint, for each aircraft of the flight. Its OK hands the weight, drag and fuel to this page and the DataCard; BMS's loadout is not changed.
lblBlockFuel: Fuel on board before taxi, lb: internal plus external tanks, less what a save's flight has already burnt.
lblBlockFuel_Val: Fuel on board before taxi, lb: internal plus external tanks, less what a save's flight has already burnt.
lblTaxiFuel: Fuel used from engine start to the runway, lb (0-1,000; the arrows step 100). Take-off fuel is block fuel less this.
numTaxiFuel: Fuel used from engine start to the runway, lb (0-1,000; the arrows step 100). Take-off fuel is block fuel less this.
lblFuel: Fuel at brake release, lb: block fuel less taxi fuel; "----" once a save's flight is airborne. It goes to the DataCard's T/O fuel.
lblFuel_val: Fuel at brake release, lb: block fuel less taxi fuel; "----" once a save's flight is airborne. It goes to the DataCard's T/O fuel.
lblGross: Take-off gross weight, lb: empty weight + take-off fuel + loadout. Red above the maximum weight. It goes to the DataCard.
lblGross_Val: Take-off gross weight, lb: empty weight + take-off fuel + loadout. Red above the maximum weight. It goes to the DataCard.
lblMax: The jet's maximum take-off weight, lb, from Falcon BMS's aircraft data.
lblMax_Val: The jet's maximum take-off weight, lb, from Falcon BMS's aircraft data.
lblDragFactor: The drag index: 1 for the clean jet plus each store, pylon and rack (and conformal tanks), from BMS's data. The climb and cruise figures use it; it goes to the DataCard.
lblDrag_Val: The drag index: 1 for the clean jet plus each store, pylon and rack (and conformal tanks), from BMS's data. The climb and cruise figures use it; it goes to the DataCard.
lblPowerPlant: The engine of the F-16 picked in Type. The take-off, climb and cruise figures come from this engine's charts.
lblPowerPlant_val: The engine of the F-16 picked in Type. The take-off, climb and cruise figures come from this engine's charts.
lblDry: The engine's thrust without afterburner, lb.
lblDry_Val: The engine's thrust without afterburner, lb.
lblMaxPower: The engine's thrust in full afterburner, lb.
lblMaxPower_Val: The engine's thrust in full afterburner, lb.
lblMilP: The MIL power setting to check on the take-off roll, in per cent, for this engine. It goes to the DataCard.
lblMilP_Val: The MIL power setting to check on the take-off roll, in per cent, for this engine. It goes to the DataCard.
lblPitch: The pitch attitude you rotate to for take-off, degrees (8-13): the higher, the slower the lift-off. The DataCard's T/O spec sets it too.
cboPitch: The pitch attitude you rotate to for take-off, degrees (8-13): the higher, the slower the lift-off. The DataCard's T/O spec sets it too.
lblPower: Take-off thrust, Full AB or MIL. It changes the take-off factor and the rotation and refusal speeds. The DataCard's T/O spec sets it too.
cboPower: Take-off thrust, Full AB or MIL. It changes the take-off factor and the rotation and refusal speeds. The DataCard's T/O spec sets it too.
lblRotate: Rotation speed, knots: where you start raising the nose, for your gross weight, pitch and thrust. It goes to the DataCard.
lblRotate_Val: Rotation speed, knots: where you start raising the nose, for your gross weight, pitch and thrust. It goes to the DataCard.
lblLiftOff: Lift-off speed, knots, at the pitch picked and your gross weight.
lblLiftOff_Val: Lift-off speed, knots, at the pitch picked and your gross weight.
lblRefusal: Refusal speed, knots: the fastest you can be on this runway and still stop on it. Red when it is not above rotation speed. It goes to the DataCard.
lblRefusal_Val: Refusal speed, knots: the fastest you can be on this runway and still stop on it. Red when it is not above rotation speed. It goes to the DataCard.
lblFactor: The take-off factor the F-16's take-off charts use, from the field's pressure altitude, temperature and thrust: the higher it is, the longer the roll.
lblFactor_Val: The take-off factor the F-16's take-off charts use, from the field's pressure altitude, temperature and thrust: the higher it is, the longer the roll.
lblClimbSchedule: The climb speed in full afterburner for your drag index: knots CAS, then the Mach to hold once you reach it.
lblScheduleMax_Val: The climb speed in full afterburner for your drag index: knots CAS, then the Mach to hold once you reach it.
lblDistance: Ground distance, nm, to climb in full afterburner from the field to the altitude picked under Cruise.
lblDistMax_Val: Ground distance, nm, to climb in full afterburner from the field to the altitude picked under Cruise.
lblFuelBurned: Fuel used, lb, to climb in full afterburner from the field to the altitude picked under Cruise.
lblFuelMax_Val: Fuel used, lb, to climb in full afterburner from the field to the altitude picked under Cruise.
lblTime: Time to climb in full afterburner from the field to the altitude picked under Cruise.
lblTimeMax_Val: Time to climb in full afterburner from the field to the altitude picked under Cruise.
lblScheduleMil: The climb speed at MIL power for your drag index: knots CAS, then the Mach to hold once you reach it. It goes to the DataCard.
lblScheduleMil_Val: The climb speed at MIL power for your drag index: knots CAS, then the Mach to hold once you reach it. It goes to the DataCard.
lblDistanceMil: Ground distance, nm, to climb at MIL power from the field to the altitude picked under Cruise.
lblDistMil_Val: Ground distance, nm, to climb at MIL power from the field to the altitude picked under Cruise.
lblFuelMil: Fuel used, lb, to climb at MIL power from the field to the altitude picked under Cruise.
lblFuelMil_Val: Fuel used, lb, to climb at MIL power from the field to the altitude picked under Cruise.
lblTimeMil: Time to climb at MIL power from the field to the altitude picked under Cruise.
lblTimeMil_Val: Time to climb at MIL power from the field to the altitude picked under Cruise.
lblOPTMach: The best-range cruise Mach for your drag index.
lblOptMach_Val: The best-range cruise Mach for your drag index.
lblCruiseAlt: Your cruise altitude, feet: the flight plan's second row, or type your own (it is held to the service ceiling). Its button climbs to it.
txtCruiseAlt: Your cruise altitude, feet: the flight plan's second row, or type your own (it is held to the service ceiling). Its button climbs to it.
radCruiseAlt: Climb to the Cruise Alt typed beside it: the MAX AB and MIL climb figures are worked out to it.
lblOptCruiseAlt: The best-range cruise altitude, feet, for your gross weight and drag index.
lblOptCruiseAlt_val: The best-range cruise altitude, feet, for your gross weight and drag index.
radOptCruiseAlt: Climb to the optimum cruise altitude: the MAX AB and MIL climb figures are worked out to it.
lblCruiseCeiling: The cruise ceiling, feet: the highest the jet can cruise at your gross weight and drag index.
lblCruiseCeiling_Val: The cruise ceiling, feet: the highest the jet can cruise at your gross weight and drag index.
radCruiseCeiling: Climb to the cruise ceiling: the MAX AB and MIL climb figures are worked out to it.
lblServiceCeiling: The service ceiling, feet: the highest the jet can climb at all, a few hundred feet above the cruise ceiling.
lblServiceCeiling_Val: The service ceiling, feet: the highest the jet can climb at all, a few hundred feet above the cruise ceiling.
radServiceCeiling: Climb to the service ceiling: the MAX AB and MIL climb figures are worked out to it.
lblAltitude: The turn's altitude, feet (1,000-36,000). The standard temperature and the true airspeed follow it.
cboAltitude: The turn's altitude, feet (1,000-36,000). The standard temperature and the true airspeed follow it.
lblGs: The G you pull in the turn (2-10).
cboGs: The G you pull in the turn (2-10).
lblActualTemp: The air's temperature at the turn's altitude, °C. It follows the standard day until you pick one; your pick is kept as a difference from standard.
cboActualTemp: The air's temperature at the turn's altitude, °C. It follows the standard day until you pick one; your pick is kept as a difference from standard.
lblSpeedTas: True airspeed, knots, for the speed, altitude and temperature under Input.
lblTAS: True airspeed, knots, for the speed, altitude and temperature under Input.
lblSpeedMach: Mach number for the speed, altitude and temperature under Input.
lblMach: Mach number for the speed, altitude and temperature under Input.
lblTemp: The standard-day temperature at the turn's altitude, °C: 15 °C less 2 °C per 1,000 ft.
lblTempStandard: The standard-day temperature at the turn's altitude, °C: 15 °C less 2 °C per 1,000 ft.
lblISAdev: The temperature picked under Input less the standard one, °C.
lblISAdevVal: The temperature picked under Input less the standard one, °C.
lblDensAlt: Density altitude, feet: the altitude plus 120 ft for each °C above standard.
lblDensityAlt: Density altitude, feet: the altitude plus 120 ft for each °C above standard.
lblTurnRad: Turn radius, feet, at that true airspeed and G: (TAS × 1.69)² ÷ (G × 32.2).
lblTurnRadius: Turn radius, feet, at that true airspeed and G: (TAS × 1.69)² ÷ (G × 32.2).
